insights.text: The 30-second film loses viewers in a way the other three assets do not. Only 52% of those who reached the quarter mark carried on to halfway, against 73% to 86% for the shorter assets, and the curve then steadies, with 81% of halfway viewers going on to the three-quarter point. A cliff of this shape is consistent with something specific in the film's second quarter rather than length alone, which gives the edit team a precise place to look. It also means the film's cost per completed view of 0.041, against 0.011 for the bumper, is not a clean read on what long-form attention costs.
